DocLints.docs_build_skipped: base `code == 1 && !haskey(ENV, "GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP") ? frozen_rounds(...) : String[]`; head adds the conjunct `all(p -> first(p) == :open, last(gate_problems(...)))`. The new skip condition implies the old one, so no refusal that failed the build at base is skipped now: the change only tightens (a :disabled or :committed problem beside an open docs round now fails the build, where the base skipped). `all` over an empty problem list would be true, but with code == 1 it only happens if the rounds changed between the two calls, in which case frozen_rounds is empty too and no skip follows

findings.title: The new public gate_problems leaves out two of gate's refusals, and returns 'no problem' where gate never passes vacuously
locations: src/CLI/Gate.jl:60-64 (gate_problems, the `isdir(RoundFiles.rounds_dir(cfg)) || return (fatal, problems)` early return)
src/CLI/Gate.jl:28-35 (gate keeps self_verify and ROUND.DIR to itself)
docs/src/guide/verbs.md:51 (gate_problems added to the public API page)
findings.before: Only `gate` existed: `code = self_verify(root; io = devnull)` ... `return 2`; `if !isdir(RoundFiles.rounds_dir(cfg)) isempty(enabled) && return 0 ... return 2 end`; then the loop and `fatal && return 2` -- one function, all refusals in it.
findings.after: `gate_problems(cfg, instruments...; io = devnull)` is documented as "What [`gate`](@ref) refuses for" and published on the API page, but it opens with `isdir(RoundFiles.rounds_dir(cfg)) || return (fatal, problems)` -- (false, []) -- and never runs self_verify; those two refusals stay in `gate` only.
findings.why_it_matters: No input that worked before behaves differently: gate refuses exactly what it refused, and the one caller (docs_build_skipped) calls gate_problems only after gate returned exit 1, which rules out both missing cases. The risk is latent. A caller that reads the empty problem list as 'the gate would pass' is told nothing refuses for a consumer with instruments enabled and no .gbg/rounds/, which gate itself refuses with exit 2 ('the gate never passes vacuously'), and for a running copy that is not the pinned one. The guard was split off, not deleted, and the new public entry point carries neither piece.
findings.description: Moving the loop into gate_problems was justified: docs_build_skipped needs the kinds of the problems to fix the skip that swallowed a :disabled refusal. But the helper's docstring claims to list what gate refuses for, while the function silently returns 'no problems' for two conditions gate refuses (self-verify failure; ROUND.DIR absent while instruments are enabled). Either the docstring should name the two refusals gate_problems leaves out, or it should say that it is only meaningful after gate returned 1.
findings.evidence: Gate.jl head: `function gate_problems(cfg::AbstractDict, instruments::AbstractString...; io::IO = devnull)` / `problems = Pair{Symbol,String}[]; fatal = false` / `isdir(RoundFiles.rounds_dir(cfg)) || return (fatal, problems)`; docstring: "What [`gate`](@ref) refuses for, each problem a `kind => message` pair."; gate keeps `println(io, "gate: ROUND.DIR — .gbg/rounds/ is absent while instruments are enabled; the gate never passes vacuously (gbg init writes it)")` / `return 2`. verbs.md: `+GBGCodingTools.gate_problems`.
